findings.summary: PM-17 corrected. Node admission consumes only a JSON document that validates against the frozen schemas/node_result.schema.v1.json; status is read from result['outcome'] and nowhere else. The Run 26 _node_reported_status bare-status-line parser is not carried forward, and no controller module scrapes a status token out of text. Bold Markdown, an explanatory suffix, an ACTIVATED verdict heading, a fenced JSON block, and IMPLEMENTED_NOT_ACTIVATED are each proven to fail with NON_JSON_RESULT and produce no receipt.

PM-15 corrected. Descendant invalidation is computed, not stored: Scheduler.currency recomputes a lineage fingerprint over graph digest, node definition, prompt, approved specification and predecessor receipt digests, checks the node's own recorded final-output digests against current bytes, and recurses into every ancestor. Changing an admitted ancestor's bytes, re-admitting an ancestor, editing the graph, or replacing the approved specification each automatically invalidate every transitive descendant, including descendants whose own output bytes are byte-identical. No manual compensating audit is required or accepted.

PM-19 corrected. Attempts are write-once directories whose terminal state is carried by immutable marker files (merged/failed/interrupted/abandoned) rather than a mutable status field; a write-set violation fails before any merge journal is opened and preserves the attempt; the merge is a write-once journal plus exactly one os.replace of a single receipt file, so no partially merged state can exist; an interrupted attempt never merges implicitly and refuses further admission with MERGE_JOURNAL_OPEN until recover() has either completed the merge or restored the previous receipt byte-for-byte; and resume() always creates a new child attempt bound to its parent and to current predecessor receipt digests.

Re-admission is a named, auditable operation. run27_controller.py readmit requires a reason code from the closed enum {INTERRUPTED_MERGE_COMPLETED, EXTERNAL_PROCESS_KILL, STATE_STORE_CORRUPTION, ANCESTOR_REWORK_REVALIDATION}, an exact --expect-result-sha256 artifact binding, a forced verification rerun recorded in the receipt, archival of the superseded receipt under receipts/history/, and an immutable audit.jsonl event carrying admission=recovery_readmission. Run 26's mechanically_revalidate silent path is rejected outright.

The controller refuses to begin or admit any non-entry node without an admitted N00 receipt whose approved_spec_sha256 equals the current digest of the graph's source_spec and whose own receipt is current (ENTRY_GATE_NOT_ADMITTED). Replacing the approved specification file revokes the gate immediately.

Attempt evidence is attempt-scoped and write-once: logs live under <state>/attempts/<node_id>/<attempt_id>/logs/, a second write to the same name raises WRITE_ONCE_VIOLATION, and a path-traversing log name is refused. The read-only commands status, plan, validate, audit, verify-live-proof and verify-final-audit are proven non-mutating by whole-tree digests of both the state directory and the repository taken before and after two consecutive runs, and they do not even create the state directory.

tools/validate_plan.py exits 0 and the complete 80-test controller suite passes twice consecutively with a byte-identical snapshot of controller/, schemas/, tests/, tools/, the admitted N00 result and its evidence, the implementation graph, and git status (24_determinism_diff.log is an empty diff).

Every Run 26 controller behaviour is enumerated as RETAINED, REPLACED or REJECTED in 40_run26_controller_disposition.log: 14 retained mechanisms (hashing, canonical digests, write-once creation, atomic replace, append-only events, ownership predicates, graph traversal, receipt history, write-set enforcement, verification rerun, predecessor binding, attempt directories, node-definition digests, ephemeral ignore lists), 6 replaced (status parsing, mechanical revalidation, stored fingerprint tolerance, multi-file sandbox merge, aggregate postmortem commands, separate predecessor checkpoint) and 9 rejected (out-of-scope contamination healing, sandbox copytree, prompt patch overlays, manifest rebase, model subprocess spawning and signal kills, parallel ready-node selection, provider preflight, synthesised BLOCKED receipts, post-merge output checks). No code was copied wholesale from plans/26_langgraph_curriculum_factory/prompt_graph_controller.py.

The Run 26 537-event audit stream is explicitly not treated as evidence for this controller. It is the record of the defective controller described in PM-19. The only evidence cited for the Run 27 controller is this node's own 80-test suite and the command logs in this evidence directory.

Scope clarification for check_forbidden_production_refs.py. It implements two independently declared graph scopes. The production scope (rules.forbidden_production_scan) reads only scan_roots and honours excluded_roots plans/tests/outputs and excluded_globs, so it never reads Plan 26 history, plan scaffolding, test sources or generated outputs; this is proven positively by asserting the exact scanned file set and negatively by planting gemini and GEMINI_API_KEY contamination under plans/ and outputs/ and requiring the scan to still pass. The tests scope (rules.retired_provider_test_scan) is a separate scope with its own roots and its own zero_occurrences_in_active_test_source policy, and exists because tools/validate_plan.py requires the owner of every migration-affected active test to run this exact command. --scope production runs the production scope alone.

Running check_forbidden_production_refs.py against the live repository currently exits 1 with 26 PROHIBITED_PROVIDER_TERM violations under runtime/ and policy/ and 57 RETIRED_PROVIDER_TERM_IN_ACTIVE_TEST violations under tests/runtime/ (30_forbidden_scan_current_repo.log). This is the expected pre-remediation state: that command is N20/N30/N40/N50/N60 verification, not N10 verification. N10's obligation is that the scanner is correct, which is proven against synthetic clean and dirty trees. A vacuous pass on the live tree is itself asserted against.

Execution model disclosure. This controller schedules, validates, verifies and receipts Plan 27 implementation nodes; it never launches a model process and it is entirely separate from the production curriculum factory runtime. The node writes its own outputs into the repository, and the controller's merge is the single-file admission of the scheduler receipt. Its default state directory is plans/27_langgraph_curriculum_factory_remediation/.run27_state, which is outside every node's declared write set and is not created by any read-only command; this node created no state directory in the repository.

The contract verifiers verify_ownership.py, verify_evidence_determinism.py and verify_requirements_lineage.py are generic, functional and kind-checked, sharing one claim engine in contracts.py. N40 and N50 author the contract YAML files these tools consume. Each verifier is proven on a truthful contract (exit 0) and on a falsified one (exit 1 naming the failing claim), including a contract of the wrong kind, a false ownership claim, a nondeterministic command, a command that mutates a path it declares stable, a requirement whose source anchor does not exist, and a requirement id present in the source but absent from the contract.

schemas/node_result.schema.v1.json was not edited, replaced or versioned. Its digest is 5ae553f83a685847542afebe084e5e7581dbb1057607f8dc5cb9208eb1f1cc18, it remains listed in rules.frozen_before_entry, and no graph node claims it in a write set. The two new schemas scheduler_receipt.schema.v1.json and attempt_record.schema.v1.json describe only the controller's internal bookkeeping and are enforced at runtime: every receipt and every attempt record is validated against them before it is written.

verify-live-proof and verify-final-audit are real read-only checks, derived generically from the graph: a live-proof node is any node whose allowed_results include NOT_AVAILABLE, and the final audit node is the graph's single sink. verify-live-proof requires a passing live proof to invoke the production CLI (rules.live_proof_cli, default runtime/run_curriculum.py), to have produced non-empty declared live outputs with matching digests, and to carry no simulated/fake/mock/stub transport marker in any evidence log, and requires a NOT_AVAILABLE result to name an open finding. verify-final-audit requires exactly one legal terminal, refuses a terminal on any non-audit node, requires ACTIVATED to be backed by PASSED live proofs and REMEDIATION_VERIFIED_NOT_ACTIVATED to be backed by a NOT_AVAILABLE live proof, and refuses to accept any invalidated ancestor receipt. N70, N80 and N90 remain responsible for confirming these match their own prompts before relying on them.
